title: Une excellente application multiplateforme avec IA native et intégration ChatGPT !
body:
Après plusieurs années avec Things 3, j’ai décidé de passer à TickTick et je suis vraiment impressionné !

J’utilise un gestionnaire de tâches autant dans ma vie personnelle que professionnelle. L’un des principaux facteurs qui m’ont poussé à quitter Things 3 était son fonctionnement limité à l’écosystème Apple, alors que mon environnement professionnel repose principalement sur Windows.

TickTick me permet enfin de gérer mes tâches de façon transparente entre mon iPhone, mon iPad et mes ordinateurs Windows, sans compromis sur les fonctionnalités.

Mais ce qui fait réellement la différence pour moi, c’est l’intégration avec ChatGPT. Je peux créer et organiser mes tâches, ajouter des échéances et gérer mes listes directement depuis une conversation. C’est un gain de temps considérable, particulièrement dans mon utilisation hybride combinant un notebook papier pour mes notes et TickTick pour le suivi de mes actions.

J’apprécie également la richesse des fonctionnalités, la flexibilité de l’application et la possibilité de l’adapter à ma façon de travailler, plutôt que l’inverse.

Après toutes ces années avec Things 3, je ne regrette absolument pas ma transition. Une excellente découverte que je recommande sans hésitation !

title: Keeps me on track
body:
I’m a senior executive assistant and over that past 3 1/2 years I’ve supported multiple c-suite leaders at my company.  At times 5 of them at once.  I love my job but it gets crazy with so many variables.  I tried many different apps and Tick Tick was the one I kept coming back to.  There are certain things I found worked for me through experience, and this app allowed me to customize my lists and tasks as needed. 
I have a separate notebook for each exec that is sectioned off by weekly meetings, to dos and notes for the exec such as travel info. I then created a To Do list with filters that will display the tasks I list within each execs folder. 
We also use Slack and having the option to add something from Slack to Tick Tick is really nice.  
I do find for my needs having the premium version is a must but for everything it helps me do it’s worth every penny (which is not much at all!).

title: The Best Productivity App Out There – A Lifesaver for ADHD & Busy Lives!
body:
I’ve been using TickTick daily for the past few years, and I can honestly say it has completely transformed how I manage my routine. As a premium user, it’s one of the best investments I’ve made — incredibly affordable for the value it brings. However, the free version is also amazing with many functionalities.

TickTick doesn’t just help me get more done — it helps me feel more in control, less overwhelmed, and more capable every day.

If you’re looking for a tool to boost your productivity, especially if you deal with focus issues or simply have a packed schedule, TickTick is an absolute game changer. The best app out there for sure, and I have tried and used many apps already. Look no further, TickTick is your best ally.

title: Best app ever!
body:
I use it as my second brain. TickTick is my go-to app for organizing everything from daily tasks to long-term goals. It seamlessly manages my to-do lists, reminders, and even helps me structure my projects with its simple but powerful interface. The calendar view is a lifesaver for planning ahead, and the ability to set recurring tasks keeps me on track with habits and routine tasks.

One feature I love is the habit tracker—it’s a real game-changer. Having a dedicated tool to track my habits within the same app means I don’t need a separate app to monitor my progress. This integration keeps everything in one place and keeps me motivated to stick with new habits.

The Eisenhower Matrix is also a huge plus, helping me effectively manage priorities. By categorizing tasks based on urgency and importance, I can focus on what truly matters and avoid getting bogged down by less critical items. If I could ask for one improvement, it would be the ability to create multiple Eisenhower Matrices—for example, one for personal tasks, another for family tasks, and a separate one for work. This addition would make task management even more flexible and organized.

The Pomodoro timer further supports my productivity, keeping me focused on each task at hand. And with tags and folders, finding my notes and tasks is quick and easy, perfect for busy days when I need information fast.

After four years of searching, I finally found TickTick. I needed a tool that could handle both my personal and professional life in all its forms—and TickTick is the only app I’ve come across that does this without being bulky. Data entry is quick and effortless, and the app is highly efficient. If it had just a touch of artificial intelligence to streamline workflows, it would be unbeatable. For anyone looking for a powerful yet lightweight productivity tool, TickTick is as good as it gets!

body: I’ve heard great things about this app, and I recently created an account. What’s more, the option to close the prompt is fairly difficult to see, so it’s not immediately clear that you can continue without purchasing an annual subscription. It’s only by logging onto their website or going onto the App Store that you can select an option to purchase a monthly subscription, and even that isn’t very clear. I find tech companies that do these sorts of things to be shady and misleading. As a user, you shouldn’t have to jump through hoops or dig very deep to find and select the subscription term you want. What this tells me is that TickTick prioritizes profit over the user experience.

At first glance it looks too simple, but all the features are there. Take the time to learn in, what each hold, tap, swipe can do, what’s hidden in the settings, etc.

So far all the things I had built into my own tracker for work I have found in this app. I foresee myself using this application for as long as I can

I will weep if this app over goes under. I have tasted true To Do list. 

There’s some minor things I’d love to see, and fully intend to submit suggestions via the website!

title: One App to Rule Them All
body: OMG this app is so good I had to write an essay about it. It does so many things but the interface is so clean, it’s kind of a design miracle. I can do everything I need in the free version but I subscribed because I want this app to exist forever. I have ADHD, so I’m always strategizing to manage my focus. Someone on an ADHD forum recommended TickTick and with some hesitation (oh no not another system…), I downloaded it a few weeks ago. I like productivity apps but if i have to flip between them, it’s not useful for me because … squirrel. TickTick has replaced the following apps for me: - ToDoist, Google Tasks - Done (habit tracker) - Toggl (task timer) - Notion (Notion is still awesome for many things, just not project management for my brain) - GoodNotes (ditto - still awesome, just not for tracking stuff) - and any number of timers and to-do lists TickTick takes my to-do list and puts the information in front of me when I need it. I can filter to just the things I need to immediately handle. I can set it to show me how long I have until the next thing is due (very helpful for a brain that only understands Now and Not Now.) It brings in my calendar events so I can see my days in context. I can start a Pomodoro (timed focus session) from within the task itself. It tracks habits and streaks, allowing me to write notes if I want to. When I reach a goal, it shows cute little animations that I like, (and I usually hate cute little animations.) And it’s got robust widgets, so good that I actually use the Apple Watch app. I actually use it on every device I own, iPad, Watch, Phone, as well as my PC via Chrome. Anyway if you are still reading, just get this app. It’s amazing. Thank you for coming to my Ted Talk.

Thank you TickTick team!

title: Academic with ADHD Approved!
body:
I’m a premed university student who was just diagnosed with ADHD and this helps me keep all my to-do’s, routine, and random thoughts all in one place! I wasn’t sure about this app at first because I didn’t know how to structure it for myself to work to my advantage. After getting a few ideas online, I’ve organized my task lists into folders depending on my needs. Free-trial definitely helped convince me to go with the pro version as the basic version lets you see your list for the day at a glance but as a visual person, seeing my month and weekly plan is a must! 
Time-management has always been elusive to me but TickTick has helped me structure my days to be productive and still fit in time for myself, my interests, and my loved ones.
Pomodoro feature helps me stay focused on my off-days when studying is the last thing I want to think about.
Many people like using multiple apps but having everything in one place for me to see and focus features really helps me ensure I’m not missing any upcoming due dates or tasks I want to complete!

Thank you TickTick for being so convenient and a godsend for helping me manage my ADHD!

body: I’m getting annoyed with the inaccessible nature of apps. I wish apple would make it mandatory that any app sold through their AppStore had to be compatible with apple accessibility features. You could get millions of buyers and set yourself apart as an app that’s fully accessible, but instead we are excluded. Your app, unlike others , has a setting to increase font, except, that’s not to increase font for visually impaired people, it’s to increase font for sighted people to be more “comfortable”. The amount it increases the font size is a complete joke for a person with a visually impairment or who is legally blind. I hadn’t checked if your app is voiceover friendly so I won’t comment on that, but if you have chosen to only make it voiceover friendly and not large font friendly then that would be painting us all with the same brush and ignoring the fact that the majority of blind people have some amount of sight. You are but one of many many programmers who have a closed mind as to who makes up society.

title: So much potential for power use but poor cross-platform implementation
body:
I'll start off by saying that this is a review of Tick Tick as a whole and not just the iOS version. I think that's important to note.

Overall, I had high hopes for Tick Tick. I thought it would have been a great cross platform option (I use a Windows device day-to-day for work) that would provide the power of GoodTask without the cost of something like OmniFocus. Unfortunately, Tick Tick proves that you can't have something Cheap, Functional, and Good Looking at the same time.

Instead of feeling like I am using a single service, each time I open one of Tick Tick's apps I feel like I'm in a completely different world. Yes, some features are only available on certain platforms due to ecosystem limitations, but that's not the problem. The problem is, the implementation of the same features on the different platforms are so widely different that I always found myself searching for a feature. It may be OK if you only ever use a single platform, but if you use more than one device you'll find yourself hunting for a feature/functionality OR having different results when using a feature. Something as simple as seeing what tasks are due on a given date is a dramatically different experience depending on what platform you're on. Like a game show, there’s always something different behind each door. 

There's also what seems like a language+logic problem. I am not certain where the app and it's developers are located, but I imagine it's not in an English first society. I mention this as the documentation and in-app explanations are not always the easiest to follow. Additionally, while these explanations are combined with the logic of the apps, the results of the functionality isn’t always as planned. 

I could likely rant about all of the small things that bother me about this app, and then rave about all of the things I like (not love). Unfortunately, the former accounts to much more than the latter.

I chose Tick Tick originally over Todoist as it had native apps—not just a web view; and seemed to offer the functionality that I’ve come to love about GoodTask. Unfrotauntely, because of the poor implemention of some very basic features, cross platform, I’ve had to throw in the towel on Tick Tick. I’ll likely revisit it near the year’s end to see if things have dramatically changed, but for now I’ll be sticking with Todist.

title: Unreliable & inconvenient NPL
body:
Current Todoist user here. I’d been trying out TickTick because I like the idea of being able to replace my calendar app, pomodoro app, and habit tracking app with just this one app. I really enjoy the UI and the UX but I won’t be switching to TickTick (at least for now) and here is why:

PROS (because props where it’s due):

1) Clean, attractive, and modern UI: reminds me a lot of Things 3 but with the benefit of more functionalities.

2) Highly customisable Settings: I like how much control users are given over how they want the app to work and look for them.

3) Swipes on tasks: I like having Delete as one of the Swipe options so I can do it fast! Without having to do multiple clicks!

4) Pomodoro timer: looks good, customisable, works well. Definitely could replace pomodoro apps.

5) Calendar: pretty advanced too, since we get multiple views.

6) Habit tracker: looks good. Definitely could replace specific habit tracking apps.

7) Description and sub-tasks are on the main task view: I like that I only need to click once to access most the tasks’ details.

8) Cross-platform: yay to a Windows app!

9) Generous Free version: surprisingly a lot of functionalities offered are available for free like attachments, locations, tags, flags, and settings options. Usually a lot of those are only made available with a subscription in nearly all other apps.

10) Good and reasonable subscription fee: around 30$ is a really good annual price for an app that offers so much! I’d happily get it if I were to choose TickTick.

11) Can reorder tasks in today view: I like that views aren’t automatically ordered by time/priority. 

CONS:

1) Natural Language Processing when adding/editing tasks: I’m used to picking by typing in the task name—using convenient shorthands—the Priority, List name, and tags. In TickTick, doing all that is a lot slower because the symbols for those add-ons are not made available on the main keyboard. So I have to click more if I want to type, say, tags right into the task name.

Now the dealbreaker—the NLP doesn’t work well and is therefore unreliable. A lot of times, the subsequent add-on deactivates the previous add-on. For example, if I write “task #errands” then write “today at 1700”, the tag #errands turns into plain text (I.e. becomes part of task name) rather than staying registered as an added tag. 

2) Selecting all/multiple tasks requires too much clicking because I have to go to the menu at the top to get to “Edit Multiple” option. Would be better if I can press and hold onto any task in the list to activate multiple select.

3)No drag & drop: I can’t select, hold, and drag a task from one list into another.

title: TickTick, you complete me <3
body: I think it’s safe to say that I have tried nearly every productivity organization app in the app store and this is by far the best tool out there. It’s not just the functionality, but the interface is clean and the themes are very pleasing (sometimes I find these apps to be too harsh, boring, and corporate looking). Also, can we just talk about the built-in Pomo timer? And the time and productivity stats tracking? But TickTick can still have fun — they’ve built in just enough gamification to be playful and motivating but still serious about work. Are these guys for real? I thought I would never be satisfied with ANY app — but then TickTick showed up in my life and was like “Hey, girl.” And I was like “Oh, hai.” I always thought I would need a man to feel complete, but I was wrong. Every morning I wake up, roll over and check my phone and just knowing TickTick is wherever I need it (phone, iPad, desktop, web) makes me feel like everything is going to be okay. TickTick, you don’t just help me complete my tasks and projects, you complete me. Xo.
